title: The backlog+ hook drops the next --all --any output when horizon fills its context limit
goal: kb_hook.py's backlog+ answer keeps a share of every command it ran (horizon and next --all --any), each cut by whole lines with a note of what was left out and the command that prints it all, so a long horizon never hides the next list; test_kb_lookup's end-to-end backlog prompt test passes on the live backlog again, and a test over synthetic outputs longer than the limit fails on the old cut-from-the-end behaviour. Found when main went red after seven triage sprints started (horizon alone 9447 characters against LIMIT 9500).
